title: The Real Difference Between Your Choices for Selling Courses Without Teachable or Stripe — No Stripe Required
author: COREMERCH
excerpt: Stripe, PayPal, Gumroad, and Lemon Squeezy block creators in dozens of countries. Here is the sovereign infrastructure that works everywhere they do not.

content.text: If you’re in Nigeria, Pakistan, or Ghana, Stripe, Teachable, and Gumroad are not options. PayPal restricts accounts. Lemon Squeezy and Paddle block your country entirely. The problem is not your product—it’s the architecture. Conventional platforms rent you access to payment rails and hosting they do not control. When those rails collapse or exclude your region, your business collapses with them. Sovereign commerce infrastructure solves this at the base layer. It replaces rented platforms with self-owned stacks: free hosting, open payment verification, automated delivery. This is not a workaround. It is permanent infrastructure ownership. Here’s the side-by-side analysis of your real choices.
What Each Option Actually Offers

Conventional platforms like Teachable, Gumroad, and Stripe offer bundled services: hosting, payment processing, and delivery in one dashboard. They are convenient until they are not. Stripe and PayPal require your country to be on their whitelist. Gumroad and Lemon Squeezy lock you into their payment processors. Sovereign stacks decouple these layers. You own the hosting (GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Pages), the payment verification (NOWPayments), and the delivery (Google Drive, Cloudflare R2). No single point of failure. No platform dependency. The tradeoff is clarity: you configure the stack once, own it forever. They offer simplicity until they disappear. You offer permanence.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

Stripe, PayPal, and Gumroad exclude countries based on financial risk, not product quality. If you’re in Zimbabwe, Venezuela, or Ethiopia, their compliance teams block you preemptively. Workarounds like VPN-based accounts violate terms of service and risk permanent bans. Sovereign stacks bypass this entirely. NOWPayments verifies crypto payments on-chain—no KYC, no country restrictions. Your store runs on globally accessible infrastructure: GitHub, Cloudflare, Google. The platform cannot exclude you because there is no platform. You deploy the stack, own the keys, and operate outside their jurisdiction. This is structural inclusion, not permission.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

Stripe and PayPal charge 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction. They hold funds for days or weeks. Crypto payments via NOWPayments cost 0.5% with instant settlement. Recommended networks like BSC and Solana keep transaction fees under $0.10. The real cost of conventional platforms is invisibility: they can freeze your account or change fees without notice. Sovereign stacks have fixed costs: $0 for hosting, $0 for delivery, 0.5% for payment verification. You pay once for deployment ($97–$197), own the infrastructure, and operate with full fee transparency. Speed and cost are secondary to control.
Stripe's geographic exclusion list is a deliberate infrastructure decision — not a temporary gap waiting to be fixed.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

On Teachable or Gumroad, your course lives on their servers. They can delete it or change terms. Sovereign stacks store your files on Google Drive or Cloudflare R2—you control access. Orders are logged in Supabase or Google Sheets—you own the data. Delivery is automated via Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script. Once deployed, the system runs itself. No monthly fees. No platform access required. The customer pays, the crypto payment confirms on-chain, and the product delivers instantly. Ownership is not just legal—it is operational. Your stack is your platform.
Which Architecture to Choose Based on Your Situation

If you need a temporary solution and trust Stripe’s whitelist, use conventional platforms. If you need permanent infrastructure that cannot be taken away, deploy a sovereign stack. The other is infrastructure.
